text:
maya: heads-up — nightly e2e longseq gate turned red, p99 spike + throughput drop. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/e2e-longseq?from=now-2h

ci-bot: nightly-longseq job #2026 failed gate (metric delta exceeded threshold)

maya: quick snapshot:
```
Metric snapshot (nightly-longseq-2026-03-16):
p95: 180ms -> 330ms (+83%)
p99: 240ms -> 510ms (+112%)
throughput: 120rps -> 78rps (-35%)
CI run: nightly-longseq-2026-03-16-02
```

pranav: thanks — can someone trigger a smoke rerun and optionally a bisect? i can try a targeted rerun with KV cache disabled. /run e2e-smoke --env canary

ci-bot: rerun queued: jenkins/runner #4578 (triggered by pranav)

ryan: i can bisect. suspect recent runtime kernel selection change from yesterday's rollout. pinging olga for infra context. :eyes:

olga: on it. which commit window are we looking at?

maya: suspect between commits abcdef0..fedcba9 (03/15 deploys). small change in kernel selector + batching heuristics.

pranav: i'll run a local smoke with KV cache disabled now and post results. if that narrows it we can short-circuit bisect.

ci-bot: jenkins/runner #4578 started (smoke). logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/4578/console

sherlock-bot: bisect job submitted for nightly-longseq across builds abcdef0..fedcba9 (20 candidates). ETA ~40m.

ryan: if bisect picks out a runtime change, we should try a quick revert candidate and re-run nightlies. if it's model quantization, we'll need to fallback to the last good variant.

olga: smoke run finished: p99 still elevated but only +30% locally. attaching short logs below:
```
[2026-03-16 02:12:34] longseq runner: kv_cache_warm=false
[2026-03-16 02:12:58] latency p99=320ms
[2026-03-16 02:13:05] throughput=95rps
```

pranav: interesting — disabling kv cache reduced the regression by ~40% locally. suggests cache warmup or cache handling regressions.

maya: good find. can we run one bisect variant where KV cache is disabled in runtime to see if that flips?

sherlock-bot: bisect: added config-variant (kv_cache_off) to candidate set. continuing.

ci-bot: bisect stage #6 completed; candidate 7 flagged (runtime: kernel-selector v2.3.1) — investigating.

ryan: looks like v2.3.1 adjusted batch cutpoints that could increase head latency for longseq. i'll repro against that build directly.

olga: grabbing perf flamegraphs now and will upload to the perf bucket. link when ready.

maya: thanks all. action items: 1) ryan to validate v2.3.1 locally and try quick revert 2) olga to upload flamegraphs & logs 3) pranav to coordinate targeted reruns (kv cache toggles) 4) maya to update on-call & mark this P1 for CI health.

pranav: /run nightly-longseq --tags longseq --override kv_cache=false (queued)

ci-bot: queued rerun #4580 (override kv_cache=false).

sherlock-bot: bisect concluded: root cause narrowed to kernel-selector v2.3.1 interacting with longseq batching when kv_cache_enabled=true. recommended mitigation: rollback v2.3.1 or deploy kernel-selector patch (v2.3.2) — patch in review.

maya: perfect — olga/ryan please prioritize patch rollout or rollback. i'll notify build-cop and update the incident doc. :thumbsup:

olga: patch PR created: https://git.redwood.internal/runtime/pulls/891 — running canary with v2.3.2 now.

ci-bot: canary run #900 passed e2e gate (v2.3.2).

ryan: confirmed local repro fixed on v2.3.2. will prepare backport and a brief postmortem note.

maya: awesome. closing loop — if no regressions show up in next 2 nightlies we'll mark this resolved. great teamwork.
